# [Baseline] - WIN - D - Network Authentication Hardening

Makes network authentication less susceptible to abuse: the system account uses the computer identity for NTLM, PKU2U with online identities is closed, LDAP traffic requests signing, the Kerberos client supports armoring and NetBIOS names are no longer resolved via broadcast.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | CIS v4 Windows 11 L1 (IntuneAdmin CISv4 profiles) and the Microsoft Security Baseline for Windows 11 — values verified against the settings catalog definitions; PKU2U deliberately deviates from the IntuneAdmin value |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Network_Authentication_Hardening.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Network_Authentication_Hardening.json) |

> **Deliberate deviation from the source:** IntuneAdmin sets PKU2U to `_1` (Allow), whereas CIS L1 2.3.11.3 requires 'Disabled'; here `_0` (Block). NetBT NodeType and LDAP signing require Windows 11 22H2 with the April 2025 update (10.0.22621.5126) or later; on older builds Intune reports 'Not applicable'. **Enforcing** Kerberos armoring (`requirekerberosarmoring`) is deliberately not included: that makes every sign-in fail against a domain that does not support armoring. SMB signing and NTLM audit are already in Local Security Policies and Security Hardening; WDigest and LLMNR in Legacy Hardening.
